obtained.how: Plymouth State University's own copy on its web site (the URL in the reference entry): a 23-slide PDF

bibliography.corrections: the document is a 23-slide presentation (slide deck), not a poster; title slide: 'Temporal Variability of Phosphorus Concentration in the stream to Squam Lake, New Hampshire during Storm Events', Anju Shrestha, Mark B. Green & Joseph N. Boyer, Plymouth State University (Environmental Science and Policy; Center for the Environment), NH Water and Watershed Conference, 3/24/2017. Authors, title and date otherwise match.

claims.claim: Livermore Cove Brook, NH: 1.77 km², 92 % forest
claims.conditions: land cover of the watershed (deciduous 60.9 %, evergreen 29.6 %, mixed 1.2 %; wetland 3.4 %)

claims.claim: Livermore Cove Brook TP yield ~0.09-0.18 kg TP ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (project arithmetic from storm shares)
claims.quote: The 3 events had made 5-10% annual TP yield.
claims.conditions: three summer storm events (5 June, 9 July, 12 August 2016), hourly ISCO samples; event yields 0.0075, 0.0003 and 0.0012 kg/ha, total 0.009 kg/ha
claims.note: 0.009 kg/ha ÷ 0.10 = 0.09 and ÷ 0.05 = 0.18 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹: the arithmetic holds. The annual yield is not measured in the source; it is implied by the authors' '5-10 %' statement on a back-up slide, and rests on three summer events in one year.

claims.claim: DOP 95 % of TP at baseflow, 50 % in events; TPP to 46 %
claims.conditions: DOP = TDP − SRP; TPP = TP − TDP; the three 2016 events
claims.note: same slide: 'TPP becomes a significant component (up to 46%) during high event flows'; SRP is ~15-20 % of TP at baseflow and falls in events

claims.claim: clockwise hysteresis for TP, PP, DOP; counterclockwise for SRP
claims.quote: TP, TDP, TPP and DOP had made clockwise hysteresis
claims.conditions: the slide shows Event One (5 June 2016); the conclusions state it without restriction to that event
claims.note: slide 16: 'SRP had made anticlockwise hysteresis indicating that it was from different source'

notes: Only the bibliography needs changing (poster → presentation slides). The slides give no TP concentrations in numbers (only plots), so the Table 3.2-2 'TP' cell's dash is right. Storm events 'contribute a disproportionate amount of P' (conclusions); SRP lagged discharge, suggesting a groundwater source.
